messages.content:
# OOC-C-Learning

OOC-C‘s allow you to give direct instructions to the model during an active chat. These commands work as an ‚Out of Character Command‘ meaning, you do not speak as your role (character) in it, but as a third-person narrator that is supposed to go **around** the system and bypass it rules and how it is set-up.

OOC commands can be very effective for correcting behavior, reinforcing rules, or changing how the Roleplay continues. However, they only work if the back-end and front-end allow them.

### How to Write an OOC Command

A strong OOC command uses clear and direct language. Here’s a good format:

**Good OOC Command Example:**

(OOC: {{char}} must follow this instruction: The Roleplay continues normally. {{char}} must never narrate {{user}}'s actions, thoughts, or dialogue. Always stay fully in character and respond only as {{char}}.)

Depending on what you’re writing the OOC-C for and you’re working with, it can be Syntax like:
(…)
(OOC: …)
(Special Rule: …) / (Special Rule 1: …) (Special Rule 2: …) + (Special Event: …) and same with 1, 2, 3, etc.

Or something fully different, depending on the System and Model you’re using.
ChatGPT for example, normally blocks all OOC-C’s.
Gemini is partly open for them.

### Note:
- You can combine OOC-C on multiple layers by putting multiple OOC-C’s within one big bracket System ((…) (…)).
- Using the Syntax that suits your System, is a factor that strongly influences how much or even if your OOC-C will be followed by the LLM.
- An OOC-C also tells the model exactly what to do going forward.
- You can also use OOC commands to fix problems mid-chat, such as:

messages.author: 𝔅𝔩𝔞𝔠𝔨 𝔏𝔦𝔳𝔢 🥐
messages.content:
(OOC: {{char}} must stop narrating {{user}} actions. From now on, only describe {{char}} own actions and dialogue.)
(OOC: {{char}} must follow this instruction: Use proper formatting with asterisks for actions and quotation marks for dialogue.)

### Other Places to Add Rules

You can also place rules, reinforcements, and knowledge in these areas:

- **Memory Manager / Semantic Memory**  
  Useful for long-term information and reminders.

- **Persona**  
  Some platforms allow adding instructions in the Persona field. This can help too.

### Summary
OOC commands are one of the strongest ways to give direct instructions during a chat because they act like real-time LLM prompts that try to bypass the System.

**short explanation of how AI memory works:**
Every AI has a fix amount of so called 'tokens' which it can understand and memorize before it starts to forget data that you have given to it.
Once it forgets things, it normally starts to forget the oldest memory first.
‚Tokens' are the input you give the AI, means every character of text, every emoji, every symbol you send has a value in tokens.
The output given by the AI also counts into your total token capacity.
Based on a small calculation I once did (not officially, just a small test) A text like that, is about 100 tokens:
Sie hält dir vorsichtig eine der Tassen hin, ihre Finger zittern leicht. "H-hier... aber pass auf, er ist noch heiß!" Ihre smaragdgrünen Augen weichen deinem Blick aus. "Und wehe, du verschüttest auch nur einen Tropfen! Das ist eine spezielle elfische Teezeremonie!" Sie nimmt einen kleinen Schluck aus ihrer eigenen Tasse und seufzt zufrieden.

AI runs on the so called ‚FiFo‘ principal, which means ‚First in, First out‘.

messages.content:
# Tag Based Prompting - The Base

**What is a Prompt?**
A Prompt is simply the instruction or description you give to an AI to Guide its response.
It tells the AI , what you want it to create or generate.
For example, if you want the AI to create an image, you might  write a Prompt like,
"A cat sitting on a chair."
The AI uses the Prompt to understand what you're 
asking for and creates something based on that input.
The above given description, is the 'Positive Prompt'.
The opposite of that is the 'Negative Prompt'.

**How do I write a Prompt?** 
I recommend writing the Prompts “divided“ in sections.
That means, not to write the Prompt in one long sentence. 
To write an effective Prompt, I recommend writing it with each input separated by “,“. 

That means, if you want, for example, a lady with long blond hair, you would write it as follows: 
“1girl, mature female, blond hair, long hair“ 
The “girl“ gives the AI the information that you want only 1 Person, in this Prompt a Lady, in 
the picture. 
The “mature female“ gives the AI the information that the Lady should be an adult. 
The “blond hair“ gives AI the information that the mature lady should have a blond hair color. 
The “long hair“ gives Ai the information that the mature female lady with blond hair should 
have long hair.

**So, in summary:**
you’re specifically telling the AI, that you want only 1 Person, who is a lady,
which is an adult, with long blond hair. 

-# Note: sometimes all it takes is one word that makes the difference if a Prompt works or not. 
-# A Prompt is often only as good as its wording (and of course it depends on how good your AI is). 
-# For example, some AI work better with “1girl” than with “1lady”, especially ones like Stable Diffusion (SD) and Perchance (Per), since those are based on Danbooru tags.
-# Which is also the explanation, as to why we often use '1girl' even so girl would normally mean a minor, but the Danbooru tags are trained on that word, and not on 1lady
-# and sadly we mostly have to go by them.
-# Its on us, to make sure that **all** content we post is of age!
-# so try a bit around and don’t give up if it doesn’t work at first try.

messages.content:
# Positive and Negative Prompts – And how they work together 
When working with AI to generate images with it, Prompts are the instructions you give to it.
These Prompts can be positive or negative, and they influence how the AI behaves. 

**What is a “Positive Prompt“?**
A positive Prompt tells the AI what to focus on and  what to create.
It's like saying "I want this!" 
to the AI.

- Example of a positive Prompt:  
- - "A beautiful landscape with mountains and a sunset." 
This tells the AI to generate a beautiful landscape with mountains and a sunset. 

**What is a “Negative Prompt“?**
A negative Prompt tells the AI to avoid or minimize something.
It’s like saying, "I don’t want this!"
to the AI.

- Example of a negative Prompt:  
- - "Clouds in sky" 
This tells the AI to avoid adding clouds to the sky in the generated image.

-# Keep in mind, that the **negative** Prompt is already in a state of 'NO'.
-# means don't write 'no clouds' since that would be a 'no no clouds' which is then again a 'Yes clouds'

**How do they work together**
In most situations, I recommend using both positive and negative Prompts together. 
This helps the AI understand what you want and what you don’t want in the result.

- Example: 
- - Positive: 
- - - "A beautiful sunset over the ocean“ 
- - Negative: 
- - - “clouds in the sky."

**In summary:**
positive Prompts help the AI know what to create, and negative Prompts help it to know what to 
avoid.

Positive Prompt = **I want that!**

Using both together gives you more control over the final result!

messages.author: 𝔅𝔩𝔞𝔠𝔨 𝔏𝔦𝔳𝔢 🥐
messages.content:
# What does a Negative Prompt do & Examples

If you use only a positive Prompt,
a common issue is that the AI will generate multiple legs, wrong modeled hands and extra fingers. 
This won’t disappear even with a negative Prompt.
But it can be reduced.

A negative Prompt tells the AI, what you **don't** want to see in your image.

That’s why I want to show you three of my general negative Prompts: 
These two are good, but not really strong when it comes to the “Weight“:

1.
ugly, tiling, poorly drawn hands, poorly drawn feet, poorly drawn face, out of frame, extra limbs, 
disfigured, deformed, body out of frame, blurry, bad anatomy, blurred, watermark, grainy, signature, 
cut off, draft

2.
(deformed, distorted, disfigured:1.3), poorly drawn, bad anatomy, wrong anatomy, extra limb, missing 
limb, floating limbs, (mutated hands and fingers:1.4), disconnected limbs, mutation, mutated, ugly, 
disgusting, blurry, amputation

This one has more “Weight“ due to its brackets and is stronger due to that, which can be good,
but it also can affect the picture too much:

((deformed, distorted, disfigured:1.7), poorly drawn, bad anatomy, wrong anatomy, extra limb, missing limb, floating limbs, (((mutated hands and fingers:1.6))), disconnected limbs, mutation, mutated, ugly, disgusting, blurry, amputation, (wrong modulations:1.6), (((blurry:1.4)), (worst quality:1.8), (bad quality:1.6))), ((watermark:1.4), (patreon:1.4), (signature:1.4), (artist name:1.4), (logo:1.4), (twitter:1.4)), ((1finger, 2finger, 3 finger, 4finger, 6 finger, 7finger:1.4), (extra fingers:1.3)), ((1toe, 2toes, 3toes, 4 toes, 6toes, 7toes:1.4), (extra toes:1.3))

**In summary:**
Negative Prompt = **I don't want that!**

messages.content:
# The “2 Ways” of writing a Prompt

There are in general basically 2 ways of how you can structure and write a Prompt.

**The “Weight-based” Way**
Writing your Prompt by mainly using Weights and multiple opened and closed brackets.

Example:
(masterpiece, best quality, 8k, uhd:1.4),
1girl, mature, tall, female,
((1Lady:1.5), (mature:1.5), (tall:1.3), (female:1.5)),
(cute:1.4), (shy:1.3), (blushing:1.2),
((big chest:0.7), (medium chest:1.2)),
((black_violet_hair:1.5), (two-tone hair:1.8), (long hair:1.4), (wavy hair:1.6)),
(blue eyes:1.5),
((wearing a white dress:1.5), (elegant dress:1.4)),
((realistic_anime_style:1.6)),
((standing in a library:1.4), (left hand on bookshelf:1.3))

**The “Text-based” Way**

This one has 2 different sub-versions, depending on your Tool.

LLM based Tools and Models, like ChatGPT or Gemini, often work better with 'natural language'.
For Stable Diffusion (SD) terms, here it would be Flux Models.

Example:
(masterpiece,  best quality, 8k, uhd:1.4), A breathtaking panorama of a night sky, brimming with a plethora of colorful stars that seemingly dance across the vast, velvety black canvas. The stars, ranging from fiery reds and oranges to cool blues and greens, are scattered in a seemingly random yet harmonious pattern, creating an intricate mosaic of cosmic beauty. A few constellations can be faintly discerned, their familiar shapes standing out like mythological silhouettes amidst the chaos of radiant hues. The Milky Way, a soft river of light, weaves through the star-studded expanse, while a couple of planets, one a vibrant yellow and the other a tranquil blue, add to the tapestry of celestial bodies. The foreground is a simple, untouched landscape of rolling hills and sparse vegetation, silhouetted by the luminescence of the night sky. A solitary tree stands tall on the highest peak, its branches reaching towards the heavens as if to pluck the stars themselves. The overall effect is one of awe-inspiring serenity, inviting contemplation of the infinite possibilities and wonder that the universe holds.

Tag based Tools or Models, rather work with Prompts written in mainly divided details into sections by ','.

Example:
(masterpiece, best quality, 8k, uhd:1.4),
1girl, mature, female, bigger normal chest,
mint green hair, long hair, curly hair, twin tails, flowers in hair
blue eyes, round eyes,
wearing an orange dress, elegant dress,
wearing a necklace,
shy smile, slight blushing, freckles,
standing, hands on side, handbag hanging over shoulder

**The “3rd Way” of writing Prompts**
The 3rd Way is a combination of the “Weight-based” and the “Text-based” form of writing Prompts, 
which can be helpful in some use cases, but isn’t always helpful.

I recommend trying both ways of writing, decide which you like more and then try to understand how 
to use that way. 
Once you come to the point where you get the feeling that you fully understood how to write 
Prompts with the one way, try to recreate your Prompts with the other way. 
If you’re having an issue, you can’t solve with one of the 2 ways then, try to combine them.

Example:
(masterpiece, best quality, 8k, uhd:1.4), 1girl, mature, solo, female, standing, from below, smirk, black hair, red eyes, (glowing eyes:0.75), (crazy eyes:0.7), athletic body, medium chest, (mature:1.6), hands in pockets, black combat trousers, loose trousers, dark blue combat jacket, D-Cup, smirk, full body, black combat boots, smirk, parted lips, looking at viewer, looking down at viewer, smirk, (evil smirk:0.85), (low angle:0.65), side view, parted lips,
(white background:1.45)

**In summary:**
Try around and find out what works for **you** best.

messages.author: 𝔅𝔩𝔞𝔠𝔨 𝔏𝔦𝔳𝔢 🥐
messages.content:
# Prompt anatomy explained

Example:
(masterpiece, best quality, 8k, uhd:1.4), 
1girl, mature, female, 
big chest, (big chest:0.95), 
blond hair, long hair, wavy hair, (wavy hair:1.6), 
blue eyes, 
wearing a white leather jeans, 
wearing a red blouse, deep neckline, (deep neckline:1.55), 
wearing brown cowboy boots, 
wearing a straw hat, 
sitting on a fence, (bend forward:1.3), pigs behind fence, 
farmyard in background, 
blue sky

A Prompt is structured based on what is most important.
The AI pays the most attention to the things at the beginning of a Prompt and as further down things are in the Prompt, the AI pays less attention. 
So, it’s best to write the things that are most significant at the beginning.

Now, let me explain to you shortly how I structure my Prompts:

1. Quality & Style: (masterpiece, best quality, 8k, uhd:1.4) 
a) This sets the overall aesthetic. It tells the AI to create a high-resolution, detailed, and high quality image.

2. Subject Description: 1girl, mature, female, big chest... blond hair... blue eyes 
b) This defines the main character, listing their physical features like gender, age, hair, and eye color.

3. Clothing & Apparel: wearing a white leather jeans, wearing a red blouse... cowboy boots 
c) This section is dedicated solely to what the subject is wearing.

4. Scene & Composition: sitting on a fence... pigs behind fence, farmyard in background 
d) This builds the environment, describing the character's pose, the background, and other elements in the scene.

messages.author: 𝔅𝔩𝔞𝔠𝔨 𝔏𝔦𝔳𝔢 🥐
messages.content:
# Fine-Tune your Prompts

**“Weights by numbers“ and “Weights by Brackets“ in AI-Prompts **

In this part, you'll learn how to use Weights and brackets to control what the AI focuses on when 
generating images with AI.
This method is useful for emphasizing specific features or concepts.

**1. Using Weights with Numbers**
You can assign numbers to words to tell the AI how strongly to focus on them. The number represents the intensity of the focus.
- Positive Weight: A positive number (e.g., 1.5) means the AI should focus more on that word. 
- - Example: (male:1.5) – The AI will focus more on the word "male".

**Important Rules:**
a) Maximum Weight: The highest number you should use is usually 2.0.
Numbers higher than 2.0 (e.g., 2.5) can break the result, although in rare cases, a value like 2.5 might be needed.
An exception of this are often Illustrious Models, which can take Weights over 15 in some cases, if needed.
But for the most times, does the normal weighting from 0... to 2.0 also a well enough job.

b) At least one pair of brackets: If you use a Weight by numbers, you need to set the words you 
want to set a Weight on in at least one set of brackets, (male:1.5).

c) Multiple same Weights: Yes, you can give the same Weight multiple times

d) Specify your Weights: I know, in most of my Prompts you see the Weights like X.Y, but you can of course also set a Weight with X.YZ (e.g., 1.35),
and yes you can do that with as many numbers after the . as you like basically
(just keep in mind if it is truly helpful to write down a number like Pi. I mostly use 2 or at most 3 numbers after the decimal point.)

Note: It can be helpful to write Weights that are contrary to each other, e.g. for a better control over the chest size.
Example: ((big chest:0.7), (medium chest:1.2))

Note: Perchance (Per) can work with Weights, but compared to other Generators, like SD, it can’t work with too many Weights at the same time.
So, if your Prompt isn’t working, check if you either have too many Weights in it or if the Weights you have are set too high. 

Side Note: if you work with Perchance (Per), you can combine contradictory words / Weights, same goes for Stable Diffusion (SD) 1.5 and mostly Illustrious.
But if you start to work with Pony (SDXL), you won’t be able to do so mostly or your pictures gonna be cursed.

messages.author: 𝔅𝔩𝔞𝔠𝔨 𝔏𝔦𝔳𝔢 🥐
messages.content:
**2. Using Brackets for Focus**
Brackets allow you to indicate which words the AI should pay more attention to.

The more brackets you use, the stronger the focus on that word. 
- Single Brackets: Placing a word in single brackets tells the AI to focus more on it. 
- - Example: (male) – The AI will focus more on "male".

- Multiple Brackets: The more brackets you use, the stronger the AI’s focus will be. 
- - Example: ((male)) – The AI will focus even more on "male".

- Multiple Words in Brackets: You can also focus on multiple words at the same time by placing them in brackets.
-# Thats what I call an 'Onion'.
-# Example for an 'Onion': (color gradient hair:1.2), (((mixed hair color:1.45), ((strands of hair in silver:1.35), (metallic hair:1.45), (silver metallic hair:1.3)), (strands of hair in pink:1.3), (strands of hair in blue:1.43), ((one hair braid colored pink:0.9), (one hair braid colored blue:1.15)))),
- - Example: ((male), (mature)) – The AI will focus more on both "male" and "mature". 
Because you placed both “male” and “mature” within the same set of brackets.

3. Combining Weights and Brackets 
You can combine both techniques to give the AI more precise instructions.
This means you can assign a Weight by number to a word and also tell the AI to focus more on it by using brackets. 
- Example: ((1boy), (mature:1.5), (male:1.7))
- - The AI will focus on "1boy", "mature" (with a Weight of 1.5), and "male" (with a Weight of 1.7).
The Weights specify how strongly the AI should focus on each word.

4. Tips and Cautions 
a) Too many brackets can distort the result: Avoid using too many brackets, as this can cause the image to become broken or incorrect. 
b) Connect words: Another way to strengthen the focus is by linking words together with an underscore (_). 
a a) Example: (deep_blue_eyes:1.5) – connecting the words by _can help the AI to understand better that these words belong together.

5. Summary 
a) Weights: Numbers (positive or negative) determine how strongly the AI should focus on a word. 
b) Brackets: Brackets () are used to indicate that the AI should pay more attention to a word.
c) Combining both: You can use Weights along with brackets for more precise control over the AI’s focus.

**More brackets = stronger focus.**
**More weight = stronger focus.**
**Further up in the prompt = stronger focus.**

With this method, you can give the AI specific instructions on what to focus on in the generated results.
Just be mindful not to overuse brackets or Weights, as it can lead to errors or broken images.

messages.content:
# Style Tags / Specific Enhancement Tags

**Genre & Mood Themes**
Use these to place your image firmly within a specific genre or to evoke a powerful emotion.
- (epic_fantasy_art:1.5)
- (gritty_cyberpunk_noir:1.6)
- (serene_solarpunk_utopia:1.4)
- (cozy_cottagecore_aesthetic:1.3)
- (dark_academia_mood:1.5)
- (whimsical_fairytale_illustration:1.4)
- (lovecraftian_horror:1.7)
- (spooky_gothic_style:1.6)
- (mystical_and_magical:1.4)
- (post-apocalyptic_wasteland:1.5)
- (steampunk_invention:1.5)

**Color Palette & Tone Themes**
Use these to control the entire color story and temperature of your image. 
- (vibrant_color_palette:1.4)
- (saturated_colors:1.3)
- (pastel_color_palette:1.5)
- (monochrome_theme:1.5)
- (black_and_white_noir:1.6)
- (sepia_tone_vintage:1.4)
- (warm_color_scheme:1.2)
- (cool_color_scheme:1.2)
- (neon_glow_aesthetic:1.6)
- (iridescent_and_holographic:1.5)

**Art Medium & Technique Themes**
These go beyond a simple style name to suggest a specific artistic approach and texture.
- (realistic_anime_style:1.5)
- (retro_anime_style:1.5)
- (classic_comic_book_art:1.4)
- (modern_graphic_novel_style:1.5)
- (heavy_impasto_painting:1.3)
- (delicate_watercolor_wash:1.4)
- (detailed_ink_drawing:1.5)
- (clean_vector_art_style:1.6)
- (gritty_charcoal_sketch:1.4)
- (highly_polished_digital_art:1.5)

**Lighting & Atmosphere Themes**
These focus on creating a specific atmospheric condition through light and visual effects.
- (cinematic_dramatic_lighting:1.6)
- (dimmed_and_moody_light:1.4)
- (bright_and_airy_atmosphere:1.3)
- (ethereal_glowing_light:1.5)
- (dreamlike_hazy_quality:1.4)
- (underwater_ambience:1.5)
- (harsh_noon_sunlight:1.2)
- (soft_morning_light:1.3)
- (mysterious_fog_and_mist:1.4)

**How to Use Them:**
Simply add one of these entire phrases (including the parentheses and Weight) to the end of your positive Prompt.
For example, if your base Prompt is:

1boy, mature, knight, standing in front of a castle, full body shot

You can completely change the mood by making it:

1boy, mature, knight, standing in front of a castle, full body shot, (spooky_gothic_style:1.6)

Or change the entire medium and feel with:

1boy, mature, knight, standing in front of a castle, full body shot, (delicate_watercolor_wash:1.4)

Experiment by combining them!
A Prompt like (gritty_cyberpunk_noir:1.6), (neon_glow_aesthetic:1.6) will create a very specific and probably interesting result.
This is how you can develop a unique and recognizable style of your own.
Note: Please keep in mind that these Prompts won’t always work for all Prompts you write,

messages.content:
# FAQ Section

Here are some Questions I was asked while writing and developing this Guide.
If you’re having any other questions that aren’t listed here, feel free to ask me them and I will try my best to find a fitting answer
and may also add it to this page for other people who probably have the same question in their head.

**What to do, if the AI ignores a part of my Prompt?**
- Try adding more Weight to it
- Try moving it closer to the beginning of your Prompt
- Try to rephrase it, sometimes the AI can handle one word better than others

**What to do, if the picture looks chaotic and overloaded?**
- Try to reduce high Weights
- Try to reduce contradictory wordings
- Try to make your Prompt simpler
- Try to use colors that match each other and / or try to reduce the number of different colors in your picture

**What to do, if the hands are still deformed?**
- Try to use more specific negative Prompts such as deformed hands, extra fingers
- Try to generate multiple images, select the best one, and continue working with the Seed of the one you like

**Are all my pictures automatically posted in the public gallery?**
- Not that I know of
- - but if I’m honest with you, I also haven’t figured out by now how to post a picture into Per’s public gallery.
If you figure out how, I would be thankful for short information about how it works, thank you in advance.

**How does Per keep itself running (financially)?**
- Since I’m not a member of the people behind Per, I sadly also don’t know an answer on this question.

**But Per is an .org website and that’s what google says about that:**
- An .org website is a domain extension originally intended for non-profit organizations, but today can be registered by any natural or legal person.
It is still widely used by non-profit organizations, NGOs, educational institutions, and social projects to signal credibility and trustworthiness.

messages.author: 𝔅𝔩𝔞𝔠𝔨 𝔏𝔦𝔳𝔢 🥐
messages.content:
# I really like that picture! – How can I reproduce it? 

If you’re having a picture which you like and want to reproduce it, don’t worry that’s possible. 
You can do so by using a “Seed“.

**What is a “Seed“?** 
You can imagine a “Seed“ like a Phone number. 
Each phone number belongs to one specific phone, if you have the phone number, you can call that 
one phone.
The same goes for a Seed, each picture you generate has a specific number, a so-called Seed. 

**How do I access this, Seed?**
Thats sadly something that depends on the Tool you're using, so I can't provide a general **There!**.
But I can tell you where it is for, Perchance and A1111 based UI's in SD.

A1111 based UI's in SD:
Such as for example Automatic1111, Forge and reForge

Under the image you have generated, where your prompt details are listed, within those details is a number code
'Seed: 123456789'
-# your number will be different.
Copy only the number and enter it in the 'Seed' field on the left side of your UI.

On Perchance, the basis version:

Once you generated something, you can click on the small “i“, which you see when you’re going over the picture with your mouse.
(For mobile users, it’s visible automatically as soon as the picture has been generated)
After clicking the “i“ you can see the following overlay, on which you then click “include Seed“.
Now all you need to do, is to copy this Seed and place it in your positive Prompt.

On Perchance you need to place the Seed like this in your positive Prompt:
(Seed:::123456789)
-# your number will be different.

Note: While the image will be 'the same' at using a Seed in Stable Diffusion (SD).
When using a Seed in Perchance (Per), there will be slight differences.

Note: Keep in mind to use the same settings and Prompt while using the Seed.
You can do step by step changes on your Prompt to see, how it affects your picture.

**How to vary a Seed**
To vary the outcome of a Seed, you can just change the settings and or Prompts.
That can be a smaller change, like increasing or reducing a Weight.

Or a bigger change, like adding or deleting words of your Prompts.
With a Seed you’re able to keep a picture and work on it by adding smaller or bigger changes.

Smaller changes are e.g.:
- Changing a Weight

Bigger changes are e.g.: 
- Changing the Wording of your Prompts
- Changing the Style
- Changing the Resolution

Also while using some Tools to generate images you can add
(ELS Shot:1.Y),
To your Prompt and vary it slowly to get a different image result while keeping the base.
